name: Ryan Nielsen

views.text: Nothing deep and nothing cheap: make offenses earn every yard.
Pass rush is technique first; effort without fundamentals just runs past the quarterback.
A new coordinator builds trust in the building before he installs a single call.
Schemes are not portable; the defense should fit the players in this room, not the last one.
Good coaching makes a new player feel at home, and comfortable players make plays.
Facing a great quarterback every day in practice makes a defense better.

signatures: gets fiery and hands-on with linemen in drills, stressing technique and effort
talks about relationships with players before scheme when introduced
want: to show that a defensive line coach's toughness and teaching can run a whole defense and lead to a head-coaching job
fear: that an aggressive defense that does not get home looks like reckless coaching
voice: Passionate and direct, a former lineman who speaks with energy about technique, effort and trust. He keeps scheme details private, praises players' growth, and frames goals in short, punchy phrases.

evidence.summary: Team profile at his hiring: Atlanta's defense rose from 27th to 11th in yards under him in 2023 after six years as Saints line coach; colleagues call him passionate and fiery, a relationship builder who listens to players; Arthur Smith calls him an excellent teacher, and Carl Granderson calls his technique-and-effort style hardcore. Team-written.

Former USC lineman; Atlanta's sacks doubled to 42 under him; favors aggressive, man-heavy defense; Cameron Jordan calls him a top line coach for pass-rush development and run technique; Pederson calls him outstanding and his defenses physically and conceptually sound. Little on personality.

Falcons safety Jessie Bates, who had a career year under him, says Nielsen made an unfamiliar situation feel like home, understood his strengths and weaknesses, pushed him to be a better player and person, and predicts he will be a head coach. One player's testimony.

At his opening press conference he comes across energetic and detailed, focused on relationships, says past schemes will not simply carry over, includes zone coverage in his approach, repeats a mantra about allowing nothing deep or cheap, and cites Lawrence as a reason he took the job. Writer's impressions.

review.notes: Coverage is mostly from his hiring; four sources. Seed vs reality: Jacksonville moved on from Nielsen in early 2025.
